source_binding.scope: src/ax_starter/**/*.py + tests/**/*.py + pyproject.toml + uv.lock + check scripts

blocking_findings.summary: An actor who can read every bound object and source but cannot traverse the only hop link can review, publish, read, index, and export the page.
blocking_findings.root_cause: Stored scope binds objects but read and publish surfaces do not recompute the stored query scope under the current actor's visible links; query does recompute it, producing inconsistent authorization.
acceptance: Recompute the stored query scope with the current actor for proposer, reviewer, draft, page, index, lint, and export paths.
Require every stored scope object to be reproducible through the current actor's visible traversal scope.
Add the link-only ACL counterexample as a regression test and keep object snapshot, hash, and current ACL checks.
Rerun independent focused tests, full regression, static checks, wheel smoke, and source-hash equality.

closed_direct_findings: B1 existing-head authorization and revision disclosure
B2 anchor and hop object binding for object ACL counterexamples
R3 effective-person and human review binding
R5 derived-output role and known marker isolation

execution_evidence.check: focused B1 B2 R3 R4 R5 tests with branch coverage
isolated installed wheel import and CLI help

claim_boundary: Passing body, hash, and executable checks does not establish semantic quality, enterprise integration, production security certification, model quality, or ROI.
